beliefs.practice: Read the MongoDB connection URI from an environment variable and never commit it to source; load it at runtime (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and, in production, prefer storing the secret in Azure Key Vault and referencing it from the app rather than embedding it in .env files.

Require TLS/SSL on the MongoDB connection by including tls=true (or ssl=true) and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in the connection string and verify server certificates; do not disable certificate validation in production.

Configure connection pooling parameters in the driver (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, waitQueueTimeoutMS) to match expected concurrency (for example maxPoolSize=50–200 for typical web workers) rather than relying on defaults.
Set sensible timeouts such as serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g., 5000 ms) and socketTimeoutMS to fail fast on network or cluster issues instead of letting requests hang indefinitely.

Store raw uploaded files (images, PDFs) outside the database (e.g., Azure Blob Storage) and only store metadata and extracted structured fields in DocumentDB to keep documents small and avoid large-document performance problems.

Model PII fields (name, DOB, ID numbers, addresses) as top-level typed fields (not buried inside free-form blobs) so they can be indexed and validated by the app; keep the raw OCR output in a separate non-indexed field.

Create a unique index on the upsert key used by the pipeline (for example normalized government_id or a deduplicated customer_id) to ensure upserts are deterministic and to prevent duplicate customers; use create_index(..., unique=True).

Add secondary indexes on frequently queried structured fields (e.g., last_name, dob, address.postcode) and avoid indexing very large text fields or raw OCR blobs; create only the indexes necessary for queries expressed by the app.

Use a vector index for embedding fields and configure its type and parameters (e.g., HNSW or DiskANN with appropriate metric and M/efConstruction or nlist parameters) rather than using default B-tree indexes for vector search.

Store embeddings as a fixed-length numeric array (field name like embedding: List[float]) and ensure the vector index definition specifies the correct dimension and metric (cosine or euclidean) matching how embeddings were produced.

Validate extractor outputs against a strict Pydantic schema and reject or flag any records that don't validate; persist only schema-validated fields and mark incomplete/invalid documents with a review_required flag.

Use application-layer encryption for highly sensitive fields (client-side field-level encryption) or at minimum encrypt them before write so that sensitive IDs are not stored in plaintext in the DB or logs.

Never log secrets (DocumentDB connection string, DB credentials, OpenAI API key); read them from environment/Key Vault at startup and ensure logging sanitizes any error messages that may contain sensitive values.
Implement idempotency for the upsert operation (e.g., use the unique indexed key and atomic update operators like $set/$setOnInsert) so retries don't create duplicates or corrupt data.

Use exponential backoff with jitter for retrying transient driver errors (network timeouts, 5xx/429 responses) and only retry idempotent operations; limit total retry attempts to avoid thundering herd.

Instrument and monitor the cluster and app: track connection pool usage, server selection failures, operation latencies, index usage, RU/s or throughput, and set alerts on elevated error rates and latency.
Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds) for ephemeral or time-bounded records (processing logs, temporary extraction caches) to automatically remove stale documents and control storage costs.
Avoid multi-megabyte documents; split very large or unstructured payloads into blob storage plus small metadata documents, and limit document size to keep replication and indexing efficient.

When using Beanie and Motor, initialize Beanie at app startup with init_beanie(database=MotorDatabase, document_models=[...]) and reuse the Motor client across the app rather than creating clients per request.
Set the driver's uuidRepresentation to 'standard' (or the library-equivalent) when using UUIDs to avoid cross-driver binary/UUID representation mismatches in MongoDB-compatible clusters.

If the cluster supports multi-document transactions and you need atomicity across documents (e.g., creating a customer and related audit doc), use transactions and ensure the driver has retryable transaction support enabled; otherwise design for single-document atomic operations.

Provision appropriate throughput and index build operations outside peak hours; when creating large indexes (including vector indexes) measure and monitor index build impact and prefer rolling/index background builds where supported.

Design queries to be covered by indexes where possible (project only required fields) and avoid $regex queries with leading wildcards or full collection scans; verify query plans with explain() during development.
